questions.text: What is the cardinal rule of an Architectural Design Competition (ADC) under SPP 208?

options.text: Transparency in judging criteria
Equal prize distribution among finalists
Anonymity of all competition entries
Public exhibition of all entries before judging

rationale.a: While transparency is important, it is not the cardinal rule of ADC under SPP 208.
rationale.b: Prize distribution is governed by rules but is not the cardinal principle.
rationale.c: Correct. Anonymity is the cardinal rule of ADC under SPP 208. All entries must be submitted anonymously to ensure fair and unbiased evaluation by the Jury.
rationale.d: Public exhibition occurs after judging, not before, and is not the cardinal rule.
rationale.correct: The cardinal rule of the ADC under SPP 208 is anonymity. All competition entries must be submitted anonymously, with no identifying information visible to the Jury. This ensures that designs are evaluated purely on their architectural merit, without bias from the entrant's identity or reputation.
rationale.takeaway: ADC cardinal rule = anonymity of entries.

questions.explanation: The cardinal rule of the ADC under SPP 208 is anonymity. All competition entries must be submitted anonymously, with no identifying information visible to the Jury. This ensures that designs are evaluated purely on their architectural merit, without bias from the entrant's identity or reputation.

questions.text: Under SPP 208, what approval must be obtained before an ADC can be announced?

options.text: PRC-Board of Architecture approval
IAPOA (UAP) approval
Local government unit endorsement
CHED accreditation

rationale.a: PRC-Board does not approve individual competitions. The IAPOA has this role.
rationale.b: Correct. IAPOA (UAP) approval must be obtained before any ADC can be announced, ensuring the competition complies with professional standards and SPP 208 requirements.
rationale.c: LGU endorsement is not required for ADC approval.
rationale.d: CHED handles education accreditation, not competition approval.
rationale.correct: SPP 208 requires IAPOA approval before any ADC announcement. The IAPOA (through the UAP) reviews the competition conditions, prize structure, Jury composition, and other terms to ensure compliance with professional standards.
rationale.takeaway: IAPOA approval required before ADC announcement.

questions.explanation: SPP 208 requires IAPOA approval before any ADC announcement. The IAPOA (through the UAP) reviews the competition conditions, prize structure, Jury composition, and other terms to ensure compliance with professional standards.

questions.text: What dispute resolution mechanism is mandatory in ADC conditions under SPP 208?

options.text: Court litigation only, which is often lengthy and costly
PRC-Board arbitration, typically involving a panel of experts
ADR (Alternative Dispute Resolution) under R.A. 9285
UAP Ethics Committee hearing, focusing on professional conduct

rationale.a: Court litigation is not the mandatory mechanism. ADR is required first.
rationale.b: PRC-Board arbitration is not specified as the mandatory ADC dispute mechanism.
rationale.c: Correct. ADR (Alternative Dispute Resolution) under R.A. 9285 is mandatory in ADC conditions, requiring disputes to be resolved through mediation or arbitration before litigation.
rationale.d: UAP Ethics Committee may handle ethical complaints but is not the mandatory dispute resolution mechanism for ADC.
rationale.correct: SPP 208 mandates ADR (Alternative Dispute Resolution) under R.A. 9285 in ADC conditions. All competition-related disputes must first go through ADR mechanisms (mediation, conciliation, or arbitration) before any court proceedings.
rationale.takeaway: ADC disputes = mandatory ADR under R.A. 9285.

questions.explanation: SPP 208 mandates ADR (Alternative Dispute Resolution) under R.A. 9285 in ADC conditions. All competition-related disputes must first go through ADR mechanisms (mediation, conciliation, or arbitration) before any court proceedings.

questions.text: In a two-stage ADC under SPP 208, what requirement applies to the Jury?

options.text: Different Juries for each stage
The same Jury must serve for both stages
The second stage Jury must have more members
Stage two requires an international Jury member

rationale.a: Different Juries would create inconsistency in evaluation criteria.
rationale.b: Correct. In a two-stage ADC, the same Jury must serve for both stages, ensuring consistency in evaluation criteria and design assessment throughout the competition.
rationale.c: Jury size remains the same for both stages.
rationale.d: International membership is not required for either stage.
rationale.correct: SPP 208 requires the same Jury to serve for both stages of a two-stage competition. This ensures continuity and consistency in design evaluation criteria, as the Jury's understanding deepens from the conceptual first stage through the detailed second stage.
rationale.takeaway: Two-stage ADC = same Jury for both stages.

questions.explanation: SPP 208 requires the same Jury to serve for both stages of a two-stage competition. This ensures continuity and consistency in design evaluation criteria, as the Jury's understanding deepens from the conceptual first stage through the detailed second stage.

questions.text: Under SPP 208, for how long must all ADC designs be exhibited, and at what cost to viewers?

options.text: 1 week, with admission fee
2 weeks minimum, free of charge
1 month, free of charge
2 weeks, with optional admission fee

rationale.a: 1 week is too short, and admission fees are not permitted.
rationale.b: Correct. All ADC designs must be exhibited for a minimum of 2 weeks, free of charge, ensuring public access to the competition results.
rationale.c: 1 month exceeds the minimum requirement, though longer exhibition is not prohibited.
rationale.d: 2 weeks is correct for duration, but the exhibition must be free — no admission fee, optional or otherwise.
rationale.correct: SPP 208 requires all ADC designs to be exhibited for a minimum of 2 weeks, free of charge. This public exhibition promotes transparency, educates the public, and gives the architectural community an opportunity to review the competition outcomes.
rationale.takeaway: ADC exhibition: minimum 2 weeks, free of charge.

questions.explanation: SPP 208 requires all ADC designs to be exhibited for a minimum of 2 weeks, free of charge. This public exhibition promotes transparency, educates the public, and gives the architectural community an opportunity to review the competition outcomes.

questions.text: Does the Professional Advisor have a vote in Jury deliberations under SPP 208?

options.text: Yes, the Professional Advisor votes on all entries, providing an additional layer of expert evaluation
Yes, but only as a tiebreaker, ensuring that the decision-making process remains balanced and fair
No, the Professional Advisor has no vote in Jury deliberations
No, but the Professional Advisor can veto the Jury's decision if it contradicts professional standards

rationale.a: The Professional Advisor does not vote. Their role is advisory, not decisional.
rationale.b: Even as tiebreaker, the PA does not vote. The odd-number Jury requirement prevents ties.
rationale.c: Correct. The Professional Advisor has no vote in Jury deliberations. The PA's role is to advise, facilitate, and ensure compliance with competition conditions, not to influence the outcome.
rationale.d: The PA has neither a vote nor a veto. The Jury's decision is autonomous.
rationale.correct: Under SPP 208, the Professional Advisor has no vote in Jury deliberations. The PA serves as a facilitator and compliance officer — ensuring competition conditions are met, advising on procedural matters, but never influencing the Jury's design evaluation.
rationale.takeaway: Professional Advisor has NO vote in Jury deliberations.

questions.explanation: Under SPP 208, the Professional Advisor has no vote in Jury deliberations. The PA serves as a facilitator and compliance officer — ensuring competition conditions are met, advising on procedural matters, but never influencing the Jury's design evaluation.

questions.text: What is the maximum Jury size and composition requirement under SPP 208?

options.text: Maximum 5 members, all must be RLAs, ensuring a consistent professional standard
Maximum 7 members, odd number, majority must be RLAs
Maximum 9 members, at least half must be RLAs, allowing for diverse professional input
Maximum 7 members, all must be RLAs, which guarantees uniformity in decision-making

rationale.a: 5 members is below the maximum, and not all need to be RLAs — only a majority.
rationale.b: Correct. The Jury has a maximum of 7 members, must be an odd number, and a majority must be Registered Licensed Architects (e.g., 4 out of 7).
rationale.c: 9 members exceeds the maximum. Also, a majority (not half) must be RLAs.
rationale.d: Maximum 7 is correct, but not all members need to be RLAs — only a majority.
rationale.correct: SPP 208 specifies the Jury: maximum 7 members, must be an odd number, and majority must be RLAs. For a 7-member Jury, at least 4 must be RLAs. The odd-number requirement prevents tie votes in deliberations.
rationale.takeaway: Jury: max 7, odd number, majority RLAs (e.g., 4/7).

questions.explanation: SPP 208 specifies the Jury: maximum 7 members, must be an odd number, and majority must be RLAs. For a 7-member Jury, at least 4 must be RLAs. The odd-number requirement prevents tie votes in deliberations.

questions.text: Under SPP 208, who retains copyright of the winning design, and how many times may it be executed?

options.text: Copyright transfers to Owner; unlimited executions, allowing the owner to replicate the design as many times as desired
Copyright retained by Author; one execution only for the winning design
Copyright shared between Author and Owner; two executions allowed, providing a balance of rights and usage
Copyright retained by Author; unlimited executions by Owner, subject to the terms of the original agreement

rationale.a: Copyright does not transfer to the Owner under SPP 208. It remains with the Author.
rationale.b: Correct. Copyright is retained by the Author (architect), and the winning design may be executed only once. The Owner receives one-time construction rights, not ownership of the design.
rationale.c: Copyright is not shared, and only one execution is permitted.
rationale.d: While copyright stays with the Author, the Owner receives only one execution right, not unlimited.
rationale.correct: Under SPP 208, copyright is retained by the Author (the architect who created the design). The winning design may be executed only once — the Owner receives the right to build the design one time. Additional uses require separate negotiation.
rationale.takeaway: Copyright stays with Author; one execution only for the winner.

questions.explanation: Under SPP 208, copyright is retained by the Author (the architect who created the design). The winning design may be executed only once — the Owner receives the right to build the design one time. Additional uses require separate negotiation.

questions.text: What is the 12-month rule under SPP 208 regarding the first prize winner?

options.text: The winner must begin design within 12 months, or risk forfeiting the prize and any associated rights
The Owner must exhibit entries for 12 months, ensuring public visibility and transparency in the selection process
If no contract is signed within 12 months, the first prize is doubled
The competition results expire after 12 months, necessitating a new competition if the project is not initiated

rationale.a: The 12-month rule protects the winner, not obligates them to start work.
rationale.b: Exhibition is for 2 weeks minimum, not 12 months.
rationale.c: Correct. If the Owner does not sign a contract with the first prize winner within 12 months, the first prize amount is doubled as compensation for the unrealized opportunity.
rationale.d: Results do not expire. The 12-month rule concerns contract execution.
rationale.correct: SPP 208's 12-month rule provides that if the Owner fails to sign a contract with the first prize winner within 12 months of the competition results, the first prize amount is doubled. This protects the winner from indefinite delay and compensates for lost opportunity.
rationale.takeaway: No contract within 12 months = first prize doubled.

questions.explanation: SPP 208's 12-month rule provides that if the Owner fails to sign a contract with the first prize winner within 12 months of the competition results, the first prize amount is doubled. This protects the winner from indefinite delay and compensates for lost opportunity.

questions.text: Under SPP 208, what is the first prize winner entitled to beyond the prize money?

options.text: Honorary UAP membership, which can enhance professional recognition
Automatic PRC registration upgrade, streamlining the licensure process
Commission to design the actual project
Publication rights for 5 years, allowing for broader dissemination of work

rationale.a: Honorary membership is not part of the ADC prize structure.
rationale.b: PRC registration is a separate regulatory matter, not related to competition outcomes.
rationale.c: Correct. The first prize winner is entitled to the commission to design the actual project, making the competition not just a recognition but a pathway to a real professional engagement.
rationale.d: Publication rights are not part of the prize structure under SPP 208.
rationale.correct: Under SPP 208, the first prize winner is entitled to the commission to design the actual project. This is a fundamental principle of the ADC — the competition serves as a method of architect selection, not merely an academic exercise.
rationale.takeaway: First prize winner gets the commission to design the actual project.

questions.explanation: Under SPP 208, the first prize winner is entitled to the commission to design the actual project. This is a fundamental principle of the ADC — the competition serves as a method of architect selection, not merely an academic exercise.
